also: how do you spend your day?

evidence: Tac. Germ. 17.1: tōtōs diēs jūxtā focum atque ignem agunt
terms.comment: With the time as its object: diem, aestātem, fēriās, vītam agere; “very frequent and classical” in this sense (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Most. 534: in forō dēgō diem
terms.comment: Most often with aetātem or vītam: to live out one’s days.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 11.27.5: hōrāsque multās saepe suāvissimō sermōne cōnsūmerēs
Servius Sulpicius in Cic. Fam. 4.12.1: eumque diem ibi cōnsūmpsī
terms.comment: With the ablative, or in and the ablative, of what fills the time.

phrases.latin: cētera intēctī tōtōs diēs jūxtā focum atque ignem agunt
phrases.english: otherwise unclothed, they spend whole days by the hearth and the fire

phrases.latin: ut domum ventitārēs hōrāsque multās saepe suāvissimō sermōne cōnsūmerēs
phrases.english: that you would often come to my house and spend many hours in the most delightful conversation

phrases.latin: ā mānī ad noctem ūsque in forō dēgō diem
phrases.english: from morning to night I spend the whole day in the forum
How do you spend your day?
